review_notes: Read the whole file and the Basic.lean definitions it depends on (next_apply is simp, cycleAngleSum_def, cycleMap_smul_vertex). Grepped all uses of the three conditional simp lemmas in the repo. isRight_vertex_pair_add_one looks fine: its LHS is in simp-normal form, it is consistent with next_apply and cycle_pair_add_one, and it cannot cycle. The weaker point is the conditional @[simp] lemma on cycleAngleSum_eq_zero_of_isRight_vertex. The cycleMap_smul_eq_self_of_vertex_eq_inr attribute is similar but I could not show it causes harm. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp failing or looping; the argument rests on how the library calls these lemmas. Confidence is moderate to low.

findings.excerpt:
theorem cycleAngleSum_eq_zero_of_isRight_vertex {j : Fin n}
    (hj : (P.vertex j).isRight) : σ.cycleAngleSum j = 0
findings.problem: This is a conditional @[simp] lemma whose side condition is phrased with `isRight`. The nearby API (e.g. `cycleAngleSum_pos_of_isLeft_vertex`) and the downstream case splits use `isLeft`. In Area.lean the only simp use still passes the lemma explicitly, instantiated with `Sum.not_isLeft.1 hl`, so the attribute does not help there. The same pattern appears on `cycleMap_smul_eq_self_of_vertex_eq_inr`, whose hypothesis `P.vertex j = .inr c` simp can only discharge when it already holds in context. No call in the repo relies on the attribute, so it only adds conditional rules that simp tries on every `cycleAngleSum` and `cycleMap • c` term.
findings.proposed_change: Either drop @[simp] from `cycleAngleSum_eq_zero_of_isRight_vertex` and `cycleMap_smul_eq_self_of_vertex_eq_inr` and keep them as explicit rewrite lemmas, which matches how every caller uses them. Or add a companion simp-normal form stated against the discharger's actual context, e.g. a lemma with hypothesis `¬ (P.vertex j).isLeft` or with `P.vertex j = .inr c`, so that `simp [hl]` closes the side goal without a manual `Sum.not_isLeft.1 hl` term.
findings.benefit: The simp set carries only rules that fire in practice. Callers such as Area.lean can write `simp [hl]` instead of building the instantiated term by hand. There is no risk of an unproved side condition silently blocking the rule.
